items.title: 2.10 Predicate logic ka haqeeqi masail par istemal (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: topic 2.10 with its Do You Know box and Class Activity (PDF 32-33, printed 28-29); the deduction diagram is ours.

blocks.text: Predicate logic knowledge (maloomat) ko saaf aur tarteeb se likh kar asal duniya (real world) ke masle hal karne mein istemal ho sakti hai. Is se hum aisi suraton ka model (namoona) bana sakte hain jin mein cheezein, un ki properties aur un ke rishte hon. Predicate logic se hum maslon ka tajziya (analysis) kar sakte hain, faisle kar sakte hain aur mantiqi tareeqe se hal dhoond sakte hain.

blocks.title: Do You Know? (Kya aap jante hain?)
blocks.text: Predicate logic khandani shajra (family tree), social networks, balkay computer programs ka bhi model bana sakti hai!

Predicates asal duniya ki cheezon ke darmiyan rishte dikha sakte hain. Maslan Borrows(x, y) ka matlab hai “student x kitab y leta (borrow karta) hai,” aur Teaches(t, s) ka matlab hai “teacher t student s ko parhata hai.” Yeh predicates saaf batate hain ke students, kitabein aur teachers aapas mein kaise jure hain. Aise rishton se hum library system ke kaam ka model bana sakte hain. Is se mukhtalif entities (cheezon ya logon) ke darmiyan len den ko tarteeb dena aur samajhna aasan hota hai.
Quantifiers ke saath logical statements likhna

Quantifiers se hum library ke aam qaide likh sakte hain. Maslan ∀x, Student(x) → Borrows(x, Book) ka matlab hai “har student ek kitab leta hai.” ∃y, Book(y) ∧ Available(y) ka matlab hai “kam az kam ek kitab aisi hai jo dastiyab (available) hai.” Yeh statements qaide aur shartein theek theek tay karte hain. Quantifiers se library system ki aam suratein bhi aur khaas suratein bhi bayan hoti hain.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Nishaan parhne ka tareeqa: → ko “agar ... to” parhein, ∧ ko “aur” (AND). Pehle qaide mein kitab ne “Book” likha hai jis ka matlab yahan “koi kitab” hai. Poori baqaida shakal yeh hogi: ∀x, Student(x) → (∃y, Book(y) ∧ Borrows(x, y)).

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Students “Tamam students ka class mein aana zaroori hai” jaise qaide universal quantifier (∀) se likhein.

Predicate logic se hum diye gaye facts se nateeje nikal sakte hain. Maslan agar “∀x, Student(x) → HasLibraryCard(x)” (har student ke paas library card hai) aur “Ali student hai,” to hum nateeja nikalte hain “Ali ke paas library card hai.”

Is tarah ki logical reasoning faisle karne mein madad deti hai, jaise yeh check karna ke koi student kitab le sakta hai ya nahi. Is se nateeje sahi aur hamesha ek jaise aate hain, aur system qabil-e-aitbaar (reliable) aur sambhalne mein aasan rehta hai.

blocks.alt: Teen box: qaida (rule) 'for all x, Student(x) -> HasLibraryCard(x)', yani har talib-e-ilm ke paas library card hai; haqeeqat (fact) 'Student(Ali)', yani Ali talib-e-ilm hai; lakeer ke neeche 'is liye' nateeja (conclusion) 'HasLibraryCard(Ali)', yani Ali ke paas library card hai.
blocks.caption: Qaide aur haqeeqat se nateeja: library card ki misal (asal khaaka, kitab ki figure nahi).

blocks.prompt: Qaida “Har dastiyab kitab li ja sakti hai” quantifier se likhein, aur dastiyab kitab B7 ke baare mein faisla karein.
blocks.explanation: ∀y, (Book(y) ∧ Available(y)) → CanBorrow(y). Book(B7) aur Available(B7) dono sach hain, is liye CanBorrow(B7) nikalta hai: B7 li ja sakti hai.

items: Predicates asal cheezon aur rishton ka model banate hain, jaise Borrows(x, y).
Quantifier wale qaide aam shartein likhte hain: ∀x, Student(x) → HasLibraryCard(x).
Qaida + fact se nateeja: har student ka card hai, Ali student hai, is liye Ali ka card hai.
